children: Revenue reached a record $47 billion, earnings demolished estimates and management added $25 billion to its outlook. Apparently, the AI buildout still needs quite a lot of boxes.
Dell delivers a substantial beat
Dell shares
jumped more than 7% in extended trading after adjusted earnings reached $7.04 per share, comfortably above Wall Street’s $4.91 estimate.
Quarterly revenue surged 58% annually to a record $46.97 billion, beating expectations near $44.9 billion. Net income climbed to $4.13 billion, or $6.34 per share, from $1.16 billion a year earlier.
Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group — containing servers, storage and networking — grew 89%, turning the veteran PC specialist into one of the AI boom’s most enthusiastic hardware suppliers.
Traditional server and networking revenue more than doubled to $10.53 billion. AI agents still require conventional processors to coordinate tasks, manage data and support accelerators.
AI orders rewrite the outlook

AI-optimized server revenue doubled to $16.4 billion during the quarter, while the backlog reached a record $95 billion. Backlog represents orders contracted but not yet delivered, providing unusually strong visibility into future sales — assuming customers still want all those servers when their turn arrives.

Dell booked more than $130 billion of AI-server orders over the past year, driven by cloud providers including CoreWeave and Nscale. Management raised its fiscal 2027 AI-server revenue forecast to $74 billion from $60 billion, after starting the year with an estimate of only $50 billion.
Full-year revenue guidance jumped to $192 billion from $167 billion, easily clearing Wall Street’s roughly $174 billion forecast. Adjusted earnings guidance rose from $17.90 to $25.50 per share.
Dell has now upgraded its annual outlook twice, because apparently one enormous revision lacked sufficient emphasis.
PCs recover, margins face scrutiny

PC sales rose around 20%, supported by commercial upgrades and Dell’s ability to pass higher memory costs through to customers. The company has raised prices as shortages lift component expenses. Useful pricing power, although buyers may eventually develop opinions about increasingly premium office laptops.
Third-quarter guidance also landed well above expectations: Dell projected approximately $49 billion in revenue and $6.50 in adjusted EPS, versus consensus estimates of $41.36 billion and $4.46.
Dell shares entered the report up more than 200% this year and trading above their historical valuation. Traders should watch AI-server margins, component availability and that $95 billion backlog.
Exceptional growth may support further gains, but a stock priced for exceptional growth receives limited forgiveness when exceptional becomes merely excellent.

title: DELL: Dell Stock Jumps 7% as AI Servers Trigger Massive Forecast Upgrade
